negative_findings.description: No BIS CPMI Red Book / CPMI statistics coverage of Ukraine was found. Ukraine is not a CPMI member jurisdiction, so BIS comparative payment statistics (cards, POS, ATM per capita) appear not to include UA.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced no BIS statistical table containing Ukraine payment-system data; BIS coverage seems limited to member jurisdictions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Analysts expecting a BIS benchmark for Ukraine must fall back on IMF FAS and World Bank GPSS/Findex; a BIS citation for UA would likely be a misattribution.

negative_findings.description: ECB payments statistics (Payments Statistics / SDW-ECB Data Portal) cover EU/EEA reporting agents; Ukraine is not a reporting country, so no ECB-published UA card/POS series was identified.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Ukraine series located in ECB comparative payments statistics during this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ECB data is still useful as an EU peer benchmark for Ukraine's convergence narrative, but cannot supply Ukrainian figures themselves.

negative_findings.description: The EBRD Project Summary Documents listing for Ukraine is a JavaScript filter interface; a stable machine-readable endpoint for the filtered project list was not confirmed in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: URL with filterCountry=Ukraine identified but not proven to return server-rendered rows.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated harvesting of EBRD Ukraine project disclosures may need a headless browser or an undocumented JSON API; this should be tested before relying on it.

negative_findings.description: USAID Ukraine financial-sector programme materials are largely mirrored on NBU pages; USAID's own document repository (DEC) and programme sites were not directly confirmed reachable in this pass, and USAID restructuring since 2025 raises the risk of link rot for programme archives.
negative_findings.result_summary: Programme content found chiefly via bank.gov.ua rather than usaid.gov/dec.usaid.gov.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Historical POS/acceptance statistics published by USAID projects may vanish; mirrors and early archiving are advisable.

negative_findings.description: No Ukrainian-language version of the World Bank Global Findex or IMF FAS Ukraine data tables was found; these datasets appear to be English-only.
negative_findings.result_summary: uk-language searches returned academic and government commentary about financial inclusion, not localised IFI datasets.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ukrainian-language monitoring must target NBU/MoF republications and academic secondary sources rather than the IFI datasets themselves.

coverage_gaps.description: It is not yet confirmed which POS-terminal series (POS terminals per 100,000 adults / per 1,000 km2, card transaction volumes) the NBU actually reports to IMF FAS for Ukraine, or how many years are populated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull the full FAS UKR series list via the IMF Data API and inventory populated indicators and their year coverage before relying on POS figures.

coverage_gaps.description: Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB), Nordic institutions (NEFCO/NIB), KfW/DEG, JICA and the Ukraine Development Fund / Ukraine Facility structures were not searched in this pass despite being listed donor-platform members.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up sweep on CEB, KfW, NIB/NEFCO, JICA and the EU Ukraine Facility for Ukraine financial-sector and digitalisation projects, in both en and uk.

coverage_gaps.description: IFI procurement notices and award records (World Bank Procurement/STEP, EBRD ECEPP, EIB tenders) were not covered — these are the layer that names equipment, suppliers and contract values for ATM/POS and banking infrastructure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated pass on World Bank Procurement Notices, EBRD ECEPP and EIB tender portals filtered to Ukraine and IT/banking equipment categories.

coverage_gaps.description: Ukrainian-language coverage in this cell rests mainly on MoF, NBU, mindev and NISS pages; IFI-side uk-language content (EIB ?lang=uk pages, IMF /uk section) was only lightly sampled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically enumerate uk-language landing pages of imf.org/uk, eib.org ?lang=uk, ebrd.com Ukrainian releases and worldbank.org/uk/country/ukraine.

coverage_gaps.description: Findex is triennial and FAS annual with long lags; neither captures wartime year-on-year shifts in Ukrainian cash usage and POS deployment.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair IFI sources with higher-frequency NBU payment-infrastructure statistics (covered by other cells) and treat IFI series as the comparability backbone rather than the timeliness layer.

brief: For Ukraine, the IFI/donor layer splits cleanly into three tiers: standardised comparable statistics (World Bank Global Findex incl. 2025 microdata, IMF Financial Access Survey via data.imf.org and its World Bank/FRED mirrors, World Bank G20 FI indicators and the Global Payment Systems Survey), programme and surveillance documents (IMF EFF review staff reports plus the Ukrainian-language MEFP published by NBU/MoF, World Bank Documents & Reports financial-sector notes), and project-level disclosures naming counterparty banks (EBRD Project Summary Documents, IFC disclosure portal incl. the new Digital Finance Future Ukraine advisory, EIB Ukraine facilities, and USAID financial-sector programme materials mirrored on bank.gov.ua). Supply-side ATM/POS numbers for Ukraine originate from the NBU and reach the international layer through IMF FAS, so IFI figures are a comparability wrapper rather than an independent measurement. Local-language coverage is real but asymmetric: the datasets are English-only, while MoF, NBU, mindev and NISS carry the authoritative Ukrainian-language accounts of IFI portfolios and financial-inclusion policy. The main blind spots are IFI procurement/tender layers (where equipment and suppliers are actually named), several unsearched donors (CEB, KfW, NIB, JICA, EU Ukraine Facility), and the risk of link rot around USAID programme archives.
